0.content:
# observAI — AI Operations & Governance

End-to-end view of the observAI LLM pipeline (**gateway → inference → Ollama**), built from the OpenTelemetry traces and metrics the services emit.

| Section | Audience | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · Executive summary** | Managers | Is the AI service used, is it healthy, what does it consume, how much needs human review? |
| **2 · Governance & human oversight** | Auditors | Can we evidence oversight, traceability and record-keeping for every AI output? |
| **3 · Engineering & reliability** | Engineers | Where is the latency, what is failing, and why? |

Use the **Task** filter above and the time-frame picker (top right) to scope every tile.

2.title: AI requests served
2.description: Total inference requests in the selected time frame (metric observai.inference.requests).

3.title: Success rate
3.description: Share of inference requests with outcome=ok. Below 100% means the model backend rejected or failed a call.

4.title: Avg inference latency
4.description: Average model-call latency reported by the inference service (histogram observai.inference.latency, milliseconds).

5.title: Tokens processed
5.description: Prompt + generated tokens. On a local model this is the meaningful consumption signal in place of a dollar cost.

6.title: Outputs flagged for human review
6.description: Responses the gateway oversight hook did not consider auto-trustworthy (span attribute ai.oversight.flagged).
6.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| summarize flagged = countIf(ai.oversight.flagged == true)

7.title: Human-review rate
7.description: Share of responses routed to human oversight. A rising rate means model quality is drifting or inputs are getting harder.
7.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| summarize { flagged = countIf(ai.oversight.flagged == true), total = count() }
| fieldsAdd review_rate_pct = if(total > 0, flagged * 100.0 / total, else: 0.0)
| fields review_rate_pct

8.title: Request volume by outcome
8.description: Inference throughput split into successful and failed calls.
8.query: timeseries requests = sum(observai.inference.requests), by: { outcome }, filter: { in(task, array($Task)) }

9.title: Token consumption over time
9.description: Prompt tokens vs generated tokens. The gap between the two lines is the model's amplification factor.
9.query: timeseries { tokens_in = sum(observai.tokens.in), tokens_out = sum(observai.tokens.out) }, filter: { in(task, array($Task)) }

10.title: Workload mix by task
10.description: Which of the four permitted tasks (chat / summarize / classify / extract) the AI system is actually used for.

11.title: Token consumption by task
11.description: Which task types drive consumption. Use this to decide where prompt or output-length tuning pays off most.
11.query:
timeseries { tin = sum(observai.tokens.in), tout = sum(observai.tokens.out) }, by: { task }, filter: { in(task, array($Task)) }
| fieldsAdd tokens_in = arraySum(tin), tokens_out = arraySum(tout)
| fields task, tokens_in, tokens_out
| sort tokens_out desc

12.title: Inference latency trend
12.description: Average and worst-case model latency. Local CPU inference is slow by nature — watch the shape, not the absolute number.
12.query: timeseries { avg_ms = avg(observai.inference.latency), max_ms = max(observai.inference.latency) }, filter: { in(task, array($Task)) }

13.content:
## 2 · Governance & human oversight

Evidence that every model output is scored, that low-confidence outputs are routed to a human, and that each one can be traced back to a specific request.

*Speaks to the record-keeping, human-oversight and accuracy-monitoring themes in the EU AI Act (Art. 12–15) and ISO/IEC 42001. The confidence value is an **explainable rule-based proxy**, not a calibrated model probability — see `inference/confidence.py`.*

14.title: Human-review queue volume
14.description: Total responses vs responses handed to human oversight. The gap is what was auto-trusted.
14.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| makeTimeseries { responses = count(), flagged_for_review = countIf(ai.oversight.flagged == true) }, time: start_time

15.title: Human-review rate over time
15.description: Percentage of outputs escalated to a human. A sustained rise is the earliest quality-drift signal this stack produces.
15.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| makeTimeseries { responses = count(), flagged = countIf(ai.oversight.flagged == true) }, time: start_time
| fieldsAdd review_rate_pct = flagged[] * 100.0 / responses[]
| fields timeframe, interval, review_rate_pct

16.title: Confidence distribution
16.description: How the rule-based confidence proxy scored each response. Everything below the 0.6 review floor is escalated.

17.title: Why outputs were flagged
17.description: The auditable reason each escalation was raised, parsed from ai.oversight.reasons. Every flag has an explainable cause by design.

18.title: Completion reason
18.description: "stop" = the model finished on its own. "length" = the output was cut off at MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, which also penalises confidence.
18.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "inference.generate"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| filter isNotNull(ai.done_reason)
| summarize responses = count(), by: { ai.done_reason }
| sort responses desc

19.title: Traceability coverage
19.description: Share of AI responses carrying a correlation id. This should stay at 100% — it is what makes a single output reconstructable end to end.
19.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| summarize { total = count(), with_id = countIf(isNotNull(request.id)) }
| fieldsAdd traceability_pct = if(total > 0, with_id * 100.0 / total, else: 0.0)
| fields traceability_pct

20.title: Model inventory — what actually served traffic
20.description: Which model versions handled requests, for how long, and how they scored. The starting point of an AI system register.
20.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "inference.generate"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| summarize {
    requests = count(),
    avg_confidence = avg(ai.confidence),
    flagged_for_review = countIf(ai.needs_review == true),
    truncated = countIf(ai.done_reason == "length"),
    first_seen = min(start_time),
    last_seen = max(start_time)
  }, by: { model = ai.model, task = ai.task, service = dt.service.name }
| fieldsAdd review_rate_pct = if(requests > 0, flagged_for_review * 100.0 / requests, else: 0.0)
| fields model, task, service, requests, avg_confidence, review_rate_pct, truncated, first_seen, last_seen
| sort requests desc

21.content:
### Audit evidence — every output that was escalated to a human

One row per flagged response, with the correlation id and trace id needed to reconstruct exactly what was asked, what the model answered, and why it was not auto-trusted. **Open a `trace.id` to jump into the full distributed trace.**

22.title: Flagged responses — audit record
22.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| filter ai.oversight.flagged == true
| fields
    start_time,
    request_id = request.id,
    task = ai.task,
    model = observai.model,
    confidence = observai.confidence,
    reasons = ai.oversight.reasons,
    input_chars = ai.input.chars,
    tokens_in = observai.tokens.in,
    tokens_out = observai.tokens.out,
    end_to_end = duration,
    trace.id
| sort start_time desc
| limit 200

23.content:
## 3 · Engineering & reliability

Where the time goes and what breaks. `gateway.handle_prompt` is the end-to-end span; `inference.generate` is the model call nested inside it — the difference between the two is gateway and network overhead.

24.title: End-to-end latency percentiles
24.description: Client-observed latency on the gateway span. p99 is what your slowest callers actually feel.
24.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| makeTimeseries { p50 = percentile(duration, 50), p95 = percentile(duration, 95), p99 = percentile(duration, 99) }, time: start_time

25.title: Where the latency lives — gateway vs model call
25.description: p95 of each hop. If the two lines track closely the model dominates; a widening gap points at the gateway, Redis rate limiting, or the network.
25.query:
fetch spans
| filter in(span.name, { "gateway.handle_prompt", "inference.generate" })
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| fieldsAdd hop = if(span.name == "gateway.handle_prompt", "1 - gateway (end to end)", else: "2 - inference (model call)")
| makeTimeseries p95 = percentile(duration, 95), time: start_time, by: { hop }

26.title: Generation throughput (tokens/sec)
26.description: Ollama's own generation timer. This is the capacity signal for a local model — it drops when the node is CPU-starved.
26.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "inference.generate"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| filter isNotNull(ai.tokens_per_sec)
| makeTimeseries { avg_tokens_per_sec = avg(ai.tokens_per_sec), min_tokens_per_sec = min(ai.tokens_per_sec) }, time: start_time

27.title: Output length vs latency
27.description: Each point is one inference. A tight diagonal means latency is driven by output length; vertical scatter means contention elsewhere.
27.query:
fetch spans
| filter span.name == "inference.generate"
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task))
| filter isNotNull(ai.tokens.out) and isNotNull(ai.latency.ms)
| fields tokens_out = ai.tokens.out, latency_ms = ai.latency.ms, task = ai.task
| limit 2000

28.title: Failure modes
28.description: ollama_unavailable = the model backend is down. inference_timeout / inference_unavailable = the gateway could not get an answer in time.
28.query:
fetch spans
| filter isNotNull(error.kind)
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task)) or isNull(ai.task)
| summarize occurrences = count(), by: { error.kind }
| sort occurrences desc

29.title: Recent failures
29.description: Most recent failed AI requests with their trace ids for drilldown.
29.query:
fetch spans
| filter isNotNull(error.kind)
| filter in(ai.task, array($Task)) or isNull(ai.task)
| fields
    start_time,
    service = dt.service.name,
    span.name,
    failure = error.kind,
    task = ai.task,
    request_id = request.id,
    duration,
    trace.id
| sort start_time desc
| limit 100

30.content:
---

### How to read this dashboard, and what it does not tell you

- **`confidence` is a proxy, not a probability.** It is computed by a small set of explainable rules in `inference/confidence.py` (empty output, truncation, very short output). It is deliberately auditable rather than statistically calibrated. That file also contains a demo-only rule that penalises any answer mentioning *bicycle* — remove it before treating confidence as a real quality signal.
- **`cost_usd` is always 0.** The model runs locally, so the meaningful consumption signals are tokens, latency and tokens/sec — which is what this dashboard charts.
- **Success rate covers the model call only.** It is derived from `observai.inference.requests`, emitted by the inference service. Requests rejected earlier by gateway validation or rate limiting (HTTP 400 / 429) never reach it and are not counted here.
- **No prompt or response text is stored in telemetry** — only lengths, token counts and scores. Content-level review has to happen in the review sink that `gateway/oversight.py` writes to.
